parts:
Hey,
I had a problem when I used ggplot2 to draw a heatmap. The  y axis always ordered reversely and I don't know why.
Here is my code:
data<-read.table
p<-ggplot(data,mapping=aes(x=plot,y=genera))
heatmap<-p+geom_tile(aes(fill=number))+scale_gradient(low="white",high="black"))
look at the picture, the y axis isn't strange?
Besides,I want to know the colour bar, ie geom_tile(aes(fill=number)), if two pictures the max value isn't equals, but I plan to put them together using the same colour bar, how I can get that?
I hope you can understand what I say, because I may using some Chinese English.
Best regards
Swall

parts: On Wed, Nov 26, 2014 at 8:39 PM, 王大万 <12052...@qq.com> wrote:

Hey,
I had a problem when I used ggplot2 to draw a heatmap. The  y axis always ordered reversely and I don't know why.

It is because earlier letters of the alphabet (a, b, c) are treated like smaller numbers (0, 1, 2) and therefore put closer to the x-axis (zero).  You can get the behavior you want by adding scale_y_reverse(), I think.  I haven't tested it because you didn't provide the data to go with the code.
Besides,I want to know the colour bar, ie geom_tile(aes(fill=number)), if two pictures the max value isn't equals, but I plan to put them together using the same colour bar, how I can get that?

I am not sure I understand what you mean, but you can get what I think you want by normalizing each row before plotting it, something like

data <- read.table(...)
data$normed <- ave(data$number, list(data$plot), FUN=function(row) row/max(row))

ggplot(data, aes(x=normed, y=genera, fill=number)) +
   geom_tile() +
   scale_fill_gradient(low="white", high="black") +
   scale_y_reverse()

zw
